# Effective cross sections

An effective cross section is what an activation measurement produces: a foil is
irradiated in a known neutron field, the product is counted afterwards, and the
number reported is the production rate per target atom per unit flux. It is one
fold of a cross section against a spectrum, with nothing else in the way.

The IAEA publishes 365 of them through
[CoNDERC](https://nds.iaea.org/conderc/effective), measured across 23 fields at
JAEA's FNS, ENEA's Frascati Neutron Generator and TU Dresden, each with the
value FISPACT-II calculated with TENDL-2017 beside it. The fields themselves
come from the companion [Spectra](https://nds.iaea.org/conderc/spectra)
dataset, on their own group boundaries.

This is the most direct test on the site of the one thing an inventory code
does before any solving happens. **89 of the reactions measure an isomeric
state directly**, which makes it also the most direct test of energy-dependent
isomeric branching: for those, the branching fraction is not a correction to
the answer, it is the answer.

yani's number here is extracted the way the experiment extracts it, by
irradiating a pure target for one short pulse and counting the product atoms,
rather than by doing the collapse integral separately. Doing it separately
would test the data and skip the code.

!!! note "Some libraries do not cover every case"

    These ran every one of the 365 reactions and had some refused: the library publishes no evaluation for an element the case needs, or yani will not solve the case on values the evaluation does not give, such as MT=5 removal whose residual nuclei it does not name. Each refusal is in the result file with its reason. That is a gap in the library rather than a gap in this page.

    * `endf-b8.1` -- 21 refused, 344 scored
    * `jeff-4.0` -- 6 refused, 359 scored
    * `fendl-3.2d` -- 59 refused, 306 scored
    * `fendl-3.2d+tendl-2025-chain` -- 44 refused, 321 scored

## yani against FISPACT-II, same library

![yani against FISPACT-II C/E](figures/ecs-summary.png#only-light)
![yani against FISPACT-II C/E](figures/ecs-summary-dark.png#only-dark)

On the 365 reactions both codes calculated with TENDL-2017, yani is closer to the measurement on **168** (46%).

| code | reactions | median C/E | within 10% | within 20% |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| yani, tendl-2017 | 365 | 1.021 | 148 | 238 |
| FISPACT-II, tendl-2017 | 365 | 1.020 | 145 | 244 |

### The 89 reactions measuring an isomeric state

| code | median C/E | within 10% | within 20% |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| yani, tendl-2017 | 1.110 | 23 | 49 |
| FISPACT-II, tendl-2017 | 1.120 | 19 | 48 |

These are the ones where the branching fraction is the answer rather than a correction to it.
